key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 steel, showing the best oxidation resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could improve SA516 boiler steel oxidation resistance through denser microstructures and protective oxide formation.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing showed severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while the best-performing coating reduced weight gain by 95.71%.
watch_item: Results cover 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles; long-term performance under actual boiler environments remains unestablished.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
